title: Coordinate multi-SDK minor version bumps and remove legacy request fields
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
We have diverging minor dependency versions across the Python, JS, and Go client libraries (http clients, telemetry libs, and protobuf/string-utils). This has caused intermittent CI flakiness and small performance regressions in tokenization and streaming paths. In addition, the legacy 'args' and 'legacy_mode' request fields (used by early adopter integrations) are still accepted by the API surface and prevent us from simplifying the client-server contract.

Goals:
- Harmonize minor and patch dependency ranges across SDKs where safe (no breaking semver changes).
- Remove acceptance of legacy request fields on the client side and prepare API deprecation notices for server-side enforcement.
- Avoid regressions: preserve throughput and latency SLOs for streaming and large-batch cases.
- Provide migration docs and automated codemods where helpful.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs (python, js, go) upgraded to pinned minor series for core libs: http clients, json/protobuf helpers, telemetry.
- Tests: cross-sdk interop tests green in CI and experimental perf regression job shows no >5% median latency regression across representative prompts.
- Server-side telemetry shows <=1% increase in error rate and no increase in 99th percentile latency after rollout.
- Deprecation guide + codemod published and linked from SDK release notes.

Planned work:
1) Audit current dependency matrix and identify safe upgrade targets (no api-breaks for pinned versions). Owner: Marco.
2) Create separate PRs per SDK grouped by dependency (e.g., fetch/httpx bump, proto serializers bump) to keep review focused.
3) Adjust CI matrices to run upgraded SDKs against the main runtime image and run perf benchmarks in a gated job.
4) Remove client-side acceptance of legacy request fields: add warnings to logs, introduce opt-out flag, then remove parsing logic.
5) Publish migration guide + codemod for common patterns that relied on 'legacy_mode' / 'args'.
6) Coordinate with runtime team for API-side deprecation window and enforcement date.

Trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- We will prefer conservative minor bumps (e.g., 2.3.x -> 2.4.x) and avoid major version upgrades during this cycle to reduce risk.
- To keep the PR size reviewable, we split by language and by dependency family rather than doing a single massive PR.
- For the legacy field removal, we will follow a two-step deprecation: (1) client emits warnings; (2) after 6 weeks, server begins returning validation error. This balances customer migration time with our goal to simplify the contract.

Testing plan:
- Unit & integration tests in each SDK run against both current and upgraded runtime stubs.
- New cross-sdk smoke runner that sends representative prompt shapes, streaming chunks, and embeddings workloads.
- Performance regression job: synthetic prompt suite (short: 16 tokens, medium: 256 tokens, long: 1024 tokens) measured across p50/p95/p99 token latency and throughput.
- Canary rollout: staged release of client packages, then server-side enforcement in low-traffic region, then global.

Migration guidance for customers (to be published in a short doc):
- Search for 'legacy_mode' and 'args' in your code and replace with the new structured 'callOptions' object. Example snippet included in the doc.
- For streaming users: ensure you update to the new client version that preserves chunk framing for the chosen http transport (note: node-fetch vs undici differences called out).
- For internal platform teams using Dedicated: coordinate upgrade to pinned runtime image matching SDK matrix.

Open risks and mitigation:
- Risk: upstream dependency introduces a micro-change impacting tokenization speed. Mitigation: run microbenchmarks and lock the sub-dependency if regression observed.
- Risk: customers still sending legacy fields after server enforcement. Mitigation: extended deprecation messaging, redirect through Console notice and email to high-usage accounts.
- Risk: CI flakiness during parallel upgrades. Mitigation: gated rollout and temporary additional matrix concurrency caps.

Links and artifacts:
- Migration doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+Minor+Bumps+and+Legacy+Field+Removal
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/912, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1445, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/401
- Perf job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/sdk-perf-regressions/weekly

Rollout schedule:
- 2025-09-15 to 2025-09-22: dependency audit & PRs opened (done).
- 2025-09-23 to 2025-09-30: CI/perf gating and limited internal dogfood.
- 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-07: client releases with deprecation warnings.
- 2025-10-15: server-side enforcement scheduled for low-traffic region (tentative).
